scope: All 111 current source identities in the length register, preserving current, branch, family and system distinctions.
rules: Retain upper boundary depth, lower boundary depth, vertical thickness, maximum-speed core depth and reported vertical extent as distinct metrics. A core depth or deepest reported reach does not establish thickness.

Use metres below the local sea surface, positive downward, only where the source reports depths in metres. Preserve pressure in dbar separately; no pressure-to-depth conversion without latitude, method and uncertainty.
Every reference needs an exact current identity, geographic support, source locator, source definition and temporal scope. A regional reference is not a whole-route depth.
Retain source synthesis, observed section, model-derived estimate and projected scenario as distinct evidence kinds. Source summaries do not become independently repeated observations.

Numeric bounds are not automatically uncertainty bounds. Preserve approximation, source variability ranges, standard deviations and measurement uncertainty separately. Never invent percentage margins.
Season labels do not imply fixed calendar months or a sampled annual minimum/maximum. Sparse seasonal descriptions do not support interpolated monthly playback.
Missing values remain null. Do not infer zero-depth upper boundaries, seabed lower boundaries, full-water-column occupation or uniform along-route thickness.
Family or system references do not fill their individual members, and individual branch measurements do not establish the full family or system.

Volume requires compatible horizontal and vertical geometry, identity, time and boundary definitions. Do not multiply unrelated length, width and depth extrema or convert transport in Sv into stored volume.
The initial register contains scoped depth references only. No reference is admitted to physical volume, state intersections, annual extrema or seasonal animation by this collection step.
A reported core-depth range describes where the core occurs, not its vertical thickness. A reported saline-flow band does not define paired whole-current boundaries.
Retain strict reach bounds as strict bounds with no invented point or finite upper endpoint.

Core thickness is the maximum vertical extent of the source-defined threshold core at a longitude, not automatically the thickness at every lateral point. Separate longitude-specific extrema and across-longitude statistics from seasonal variability and uncertainty.
Explicit source months may be retained with a calendar locator; never infer month membership from a season label alone.
Freeze previous source facts and registers. Preserve the entire preceding evidence list before appending qualified references.

The source-selected vertical domain of an inverse-model transport section is a distinct depth metric. Retain its station/layer selection and reported depth cells; density surfaces need not have uniform metre depths across the section.
A section-sampling window dates the entire section, not the selected boundary stations. An inverse-model decade group is not a decade mean, annual envelope or repeated monthly sampling.
A common source row may link width and depth extents, but their product is not cross-sectional area without the vertical and lateral shape. No rectangle or volume is inferred.

Retain a source strict upper bound as upper_bound_m with upper_bound_exclusive=true. This is a one-sided bound on the numeric depth metric, not the upper flow boundary; do not convert it to a point, a zero-to-bound thickness, a confidence interval or an annual maximum.
Retain overlapping observation records as overlapping cases. Different averaging methods, spatial sections or periods do not establish independent repeats or a temporal/error range.

A source statement that flow continues below its sampling limit may support a strict lower bound on reported reach; the sampling limit itself does not become a detected flow boundary. Model and observational extents remain separately qualified.

An inverse-transport domain stated as a numeric top to bottom retains its numeric top as transport_selected_upper_depth and its lower terminal as seafloor_unspecified_numeric_depth. This is not a whole-current upper flow boundary. Never substitute bathymetry or an invented bottom depth, or subtract it to infer thickness.

Printed table numbers and XML table-wrap IDs differ. Preserve the printed table number, XML ID, one-based tbody row, column and group row explicitly rather than treating XML IDs as printed table numbers.
Distinct cross-shore descriptions are spatial support, not annual or uncertainty bounds. A front or deep component reference does not establish the complete current system.

Thickness is a distance, not a depth datum. New reported_vertical_thickness references use not_applicable_thickness_distance rather than a sea-surface datum. A source may report regional or section-specific thickness directly. Retain it as reported_vertical_thickness with its evidence kind and support, distinct from bottom depth, core depth and whole-route thickness. Do not assign it to the whole-current thickness_m field or derive paired boundaries without evidence.

For a diagnosed core retain the complete selection operator: velocity isotach, or water-mass filter plus transport-ranked mean mask, including imposed analysis cutoffs. An imposed50m analysis boundary is not the physical upper flow boundary.
Retain a source metre statement in metres and nearby pressure statements separately. Equal numerical values do not authorize pressure-to-depth conversion.

Preserve inclusive at-least lower bounds with lower_bound_operator >= and lower_bound_exclusive=false. Distinguish them from strict greater-than bounds, numeric points, exact bottom depths and intervals. Source language determines inclusivity.
Core depth must retain which field defines the core. A thermohaline maximum is not a maximum-speed core or full-flow boundary; source-defined current water-mass context is kept explicit.

Multiple jets within a source current identity retain separate branch labels and reconstructed-velocity methods. Neither a sampled depth limit nor another model product establishes their physical bottom.

A reference for a named seasonal branch may be attached to its catalogued parent only with an explicit partial_seasonal_branch scope. It does not fill other seasons, adjacent currents described as similar, generic families or whole-route geometry.

Different regional depths within one campaign are spatial variation, not temporal extrema or independent annual repeats. Keep month-precision campaign bounds distinct from unknown exact section dates.

State whether evidence comes from original article pages, full publisher HTML or publisher abstract. Abstract-only support may preserve explicitly stated regional numbers but cannot supply unreviewed full-paper definitions.

Distinguish calendar years from simulation years in a climatological experiment. An eight-year spin-up analysed over its final three years does not inherit calendar years from satellite validation or atmospheric forcing products. Record the model time basis explicitly.

A direction-reversal depth may describe the bottom of a seasonal directional component even when transport integration extends deeper through opposing flow. Keep the directional component, months and reversal definition explicit; do not use the integration cutoff as its physical boundary.
Regional averaging can yield a core-depth band or a layer where flow is mainly concentrated. Neither is a route profile, an annual envelope or evidence of zero flow below the reported layer.

Distinguish a reported range of lower reach scales from an occupied depth band. A surface current reaching1000–1200m does not occupy only that subsurface band; an upper-layer scale50–100m does not place its top at50m.

A water-mass-selected stream-tube domain retains its full vertical and lateral selection definitions and branch scope. An approximate reported domain does not become paired whole-flow boundaries, a pointwise thickness field or the nearby water-mass table interval.

A range across salinity maxima of distinct equilibrated outflow product waters is a range across property-defined cores. It does not describe the thickness of one continuous layer, a speed maximum or seasonal core migration.

A depth used to classify a surface current separately from an undercurrent is a source convention, not a detected no-flow boundary. Keep depth_basis explicit and do not transfer deeper undercurrent anomalies to the surface-current identity.

When a source reports current reach to its sampling limit, preserve that reported value together with the sampling limit and a false sampling_limit_is_flow_boundary flag. Do not infer a detected bottom, flow cessation, greater reach or whole-route thickness.
Mean sections from one mooring array retain their longitude and own averaging months. Longer nearby mooring records or event-composite periods do not date the shorter array mean.

Depth where laterally integrated net section transport reaches zero is a transport diagnostic. Preserve lateral selection, eddy cancellations, exclusions, reconstruction and section location. It does not imply every point across that section has zero velocity or a common physical current bottom.

Use a comparison figure caption to date the mean profile plotted there. An overall longer observing span mentioned in the text does not establish that same averaging interval or continuous coverage. Preserve both supports separately.

An author explicitly distinguishing a transport integration limit from unknown total current extent must retain that distinction. A historical unknown is dated to the source, not generalized to all subsequent knowledge.

An OSW-derived directional velocity-layer crossing is a local diagnostic, not a unique physical boundary of the named current. Preserve measurement ID, profile index, coordinates, actual interval, source timestamp, derived representative time, velocity threshold, minimum support, operator hash and source dataset. Preserve unresolved opposite boundaries and threshold comparisons through the measurement join. Do not turn a sampling bracket into a confidence interval or pool sequential sections into annual extrema.

Water-mass depth bands belong to the explicitly named component. Resolve source abbreviations before joining: AW in Carroll2018 is Arctic water, not Atlantic water. Do not substitute regional basin or sill depth for flow depth.

Qualitative near-halt depth is a separate reported_near_zero_flow_depth metric. Preserve the absence of a numerical threshold and exact-zero evidence. Do not infer full current bottom, thickness, or convert a pycnocline or instrument depth into this metric.

A literature seasonal description for a parent current system may be retained as explicit parent-system context for a catalogued regional segment, with that scope relationship recorded. It does not establish a profile of the segment or of the wider system. Do not date the literature statement to a separate experiment in the same paper or map season labels to unreported months.

Author-selected isotach boundaries retain velocity threshold, reconstruction and reference levels. Geostrophic no-motion reference pressure and ADCP reference depth are processing assumptions, not measured current boundaries. Distinguish contemporaneous section differences from temporal extrema; keep one author group summary as one reference rather than manufacturing independent sections.

For a current system retain the specific coastal, offshore, undercurrent or countercurrent branch on each depth reference. A sequence of branch sections is not the depth of every branch or the whole reference route. Source-reported isotach depths must be distinguished from separate theoretical predictions shown in the same figure.

Model analysis years are elapsed simulation indices unless explicitly dated. Climatological forcing and archive release/version years do not establish observation years. Keep model/observational reconstructions and noncontemporaneous depth cases separate.

A flow component reported at a depth can support an explicitly inferred inclusive reach bound at that depth, not a strict greater-than bound or terminal boundary. Check original PDF prose when indexed text disagrees about an inequality symbol. Deep recirculation or eddy influence must remain explicit; do not inherit depths into separately named downstream currents.

Monthly velocity-profile maxima retain the valid depth domain and whether the maximum lies at the shallowest retained sample. An edge maximum does not resolve a shallower unsampled core. Preserve instrument gaps, short-record/interannual contamination and processing; explicit month labels do not establish annual extrema or seasonal playback eligibility.

An approximate current extent may be supported by opposing shallow/deep flow observations and an author-selected no-motion reference. Preserve which depth is a processing choice and state that exact zero was not observed. Do not count geostrophy or SSH products sharing that reference as independent confirmation of an exact boundary.

A broad current name covering an Australian boundary branch and PNG arc must retain the branch on each depth value. A deeper-than lower reach bound is not a terminal depth, and a separate transport integration domain is not a measured flow bottom.

A source-reported vertical scale length is a distance metric using not_applicable_scale_distance, distinct from core depth, terminal depth and thickness. If its operational definition has not been recovered, retain that limitation; do not assume exponential decay or convert the scale to a boundary or volume.

Resolve current names against source latitude, branch geography and catalog convention before admission. The subtropical South Indian Countercurrent around22–30S is not the Indian South Equatorial Countercurrent near4–10S. Historical West Australian Current cyclonic-stream descriptions must retain their regional convention instead of being generalized to the full modern offshore gyre-return corridor.

Persistence of reconstructed flow features at a mapped depth supports an explicitly inferred inclusive reach bound, not a terminal boundary. Preserve assumed geostrophic reference pressure, whole-cruise temporal support and spatial weakening; do not convert reference pressure to depth or claim direct velocities.

Water-mass layer depths retain their water-mass definition and region; they are not automatically kinematic flow boundaries. Spatial basin differences do not establish temporal ranges or thickness for all named-current branches.

Transport-selected cores may use different ranking operators in different sections of one source. Preserve BSO salinity ranking separately from velocity ranking at adjacent slope sections, including the mean-mask fraction and imposed shallow cutoff. A source name for a branch must be explicitly mapped before admission.

Depth evidence outside an editorial reference route can be retained as explicitly conditional regional context. Mark it ineligible for projection onto that reference route; do not extend its support merely to fill a route-depth gap. Nearby bathymetry or a separate model run does not date or define the literature flow layer.

A source-described dominant flow layer retains any unquantified dominance fraction. Primarily above a depth does not establish a terminal flow boundary, a specified transport percentile or a uniformly filled section. Preserve assumed no-motion reference levels and uneven multicruise support separately; a list of cruises is not continuous coverage.

A water-mass band explicitly attributed to a current may be retained as component evidence. Keep occupied-depth intervals distinct from variable bottom-depth intervals and do not transfer an adjacent differently attributed component. Modern physical-setting literature in a paleoclimate paper is not dated to the paleorecord, publication year or nearby sediment-site bathymetry.

A nonzero speed or source flow statement at a specified depth supports an explicitly inferred inclusive reach bound, with any cited speed/fraction retained as context. It does not establish terminal depth, an exponential scale or a uniform profile. An unlocated illustrative profile is not spatially projectable onto a declared reference route.

A water-mass interface between opposing current systems is a component depth diagnostic, not necessarily a kinematic flow boundary. Preserve the studied limb, regional exceptions and source season. Evidence for the southern limb does not cover the western limb of a composite system; summer component context does not establish the catalog winter linkage. Seasonal summaries without repeated section/time support are not annual envelopes.

A published composite-section mean depth may retain its source-reported spatial range as a separate attribute. Neither is a time envelope, a confidence interval, a deepest-flow boundary or the imposed geostrophic reference. Preserve the salinity or velocity operator selecting the depth.

A same-source depth/width join requires identical current identity, section, source table row, temporal operator, lateral selection, integration base and geostrophic reference, with pinned original inventory/audit pointers. Retain profile-count discrepancies. Matching source rows alone do not establish the weighting behind a published mean or justify rectangular area/volume; those eligibility claims require their own evidence.

A sampled_water_mass_depth_band describes depths of samples assigned to a water-mass component. Preserve campaign window and classification properties. Endpoints are not physical upper/lower flow boundaries, continuity is not implied, and subtracting endpoints does not establish current thickness. Do not promote a sampled classification to a velocity layer.

Qualitative flow presence read from an original velocity-profile figure may support an explicitly conservative inclusive reach bound at a labeled depth. Preserve panel, observed/model series, coordinate convention and averaging period. Distinguish mean vectors from variability ellipses. Such a reading does not digitize speed, establish statistical significance, identify terminal depth, or prove instantaneous/seasonal coverage; station bathymetry is not the inferred flow depth.

A named-current record at a stated instrument depth supports only an explicitly inferred inclusive reach bound. Preserve station, position, averaging and original observing year. Adjacent panels, unrelated current records and geostrophic no-motion references do not supply a deeper bound.

When source whole-column flow is reported for a depth-limited ADCP, constrain the reach inference to the deepest valid sample. Preserve valid depth range, instrument mounting depth, station bathymetry and regime dates separately. Source challenges to current persistence must remain explicit; no regional episodic flow may be promoted to a permanent annual named current.

Regional velocity-core depths along a jet retain main/secondary branch, source averaging or fitting operator and uneven temporal sampling. Spatial shoaling is not an annual depth range or flow thickness. Do not combine neighboring-current cores, latitude summaries from another longitude, or introductory shorthand with the numerical results section. Overlapping historical archives are not independent confirmation.

A reach statement qualified by a speed threshold retains the threshold and strict/inclusive inequality. A joint observational-section/model-month summary is one comparison reference, not independent replicate evidence. Preserve elapsed model year separately from observing calendar dates. Regional branch evidence outside the selected route cannot be projected onto that route.

A qualitative signed-velocity section reading requires the original figure, labeled depth, sign convention, current identity from spatial context and explicit separation of observation/model panels. It may support an inclusive reach inference, not a speed measurement, significance result or terminal boundary. Depth averaging windows, nominal model layer thickness and instrument range must not be substituted for physical flow depth. Preserve approximate figure neighborhood and whole-campaign dates without inventing precise station occupations.

Historical current synonyms require an explicit same-source direction/geography mapping, retaining any combined-name convention. A named geostrophic curve may support inclusive presence at a labeled depth, without recovering absolute velocity or exact reference level. Keep unlocated undated illustrations non-projectable; neighboring curves, prose speed ratios, figure endpoints and general methodological references are not transferable measurements.

A conditional regional identity mapping preserves source direction and geography without equating an entire broader current with a narrower glossary usage. Source depth-dependent flow behavior within a sampling domain supports only the stated conservative reach inference; domain endpoints, bathymetry and separate-year/deep instruments remain distinct.

Family/system depth discovery links existing member-owned references under pinned catalog conventions. It does not copy numerical depths, count new measurements, choose the deepest/longest member as a parent depth, combine incompatible metrics or sum overlapping parents and children. Missing members remain explicit, and a linked parent is not a measured whole system.

An approximate nonzero-flow depth described as nearly a value remains an approximate presence-depth descriptor, not an inclusive reach bound at that rounded value or terminal boundary. A reported approximate extent-depth interval is distinct from an occupied top/bottom band; subtracting its endpoints does not give current thickness. Separate dates, regional intersections, adjacent eddies, water-property depths, transport domains and variable geostrophic references.

An author regional depth summary spanning multiple surveys is one reference unless separate depths are explicitly established. Retain each survey period/season without inventing one continuous observation period or annual envelope. A current-speed magnitude profile cannot establish westward direction or a zonal zero crossing; retain the author prose identity and depth statement separately. Velocity standard deviations are not depth uncertainty, and instrument/display/biological sampling limits are not current boundaries.

A comparison-selected core level near a broad velocity maximum retains its ADCP/model selection criterion and site-specific record window with gaps. It is not a newly diagnosed instantaneous core, exact unbiased observed maximum, common-period climatology or current bottom. Raw bin size, processed level spacing, velocity equivalence tolerance and sampling-domain limits are separate from depth uncertainty and physical boundaries. A later spatial interpolation of differing record means must retain every site period and be labeled noncontemporaneous.

An observed multi-cruise core, an interannually forced model-period core and a repeating-forcing spin-up core are separate cases even at the same longitude. Interpolate only matching model/mean definitions and periods; retain observation/model discrepancies. Nominal equatorial section-connector geometry cannot establish an exact off-equatorial core latitude. Transport integration domains, surface-mean completion and model vertical resolution do not supply physical layer boundaries or depth uncertainty.

All core_vertical_thickness references use not_applicable_thickness_distance: maximum vertical span is a distance, not an absolute depth below the sea surface. A versioned normalization may correct legacy metadata only with exact prior-reference hashes, original datum retained and numerical/source fields unchanged. A threshold-core vertical span need not describe a filled contiguous column, full-flow thickness or a lower-boundary depth.

Maximum depth and cross-sectional area of the same fixed mean-velocity isotach mask may support a separately reviewed regional geometry scenario. Preserve signed velocity, period, mean-mask versus instantaneous-mask distinction and section orientation. Offshore distance is not current width. Regional integration needs an explicit along-route geometry/orientation assumption and must not extend past selected current gates or become a whole-current volume or a mean instantaneous volume.

A source-reported flow presence at a named depth supports an inclusive minimum reach (>=), not a detected lower boundary or thickness. Preserve the averaging coordinate frame and deployment precision. A width reported at a deep level is depth-specific context, not a surface or whole-current width; presence and deep width alone cannot establish cross-sectional area or volume. Abstract-only review must remain explicitly labeled.

derived_mean_velocity_zero_crossing_depth is an OSW-calculated local descriptor of an explicitly processed velocity mean, not a published physical boundary or thickness. Preserve averaging order, coordinate rotation, source flags, exact product hash and per-month support. Separate near-halt velocity contours from strict zero crossings, and separate zero of mean from mean instantaneous boundary. A failed strict crossing leaves boundary depth unknown; do not substitute a sampling limit, local velocity extremum, velocity tolerance or seasonal interpolation. Sampling brackets, alternate averaging methods and display rounding are not confidence intervals.

Source-reported section area may supplement an existing depth reference through an explicit same-section/same-mask/period link without rewriting the historical depth reference. Preserve approximate area precision, cell geometry bias and local selection-domain differences. A source heat-budget box area/depth/volume is a separate idealization, not the actual current mask geometry. A reported inter-section path length may parameterize an explicitly assumed regional extrusion without supplying map coordinates or a whole-current route.

Noncontemporaneous mooring means processed in one published framework may support a separately labeled historical reference-connector scenario with every site period and reliability flag retained. They are not a common-period climatology, simultaneous transect or seasonal envelope. An intervening low-significance source anchor must be flagged rather than silently dropped. Modal reconstruction, instrument sampling limits, bathymetry, hydrographic reference levels and velocity-error intervals are distinct from author-reported mean current extent.

Source-reported pressure reversals may enter the metre register only as explicitly converted descriptors with native reference/value/unit, latitude rule, pinned conversion method, pressure-datum assumption, geopotential assumptions, rounding and uncertainty status retained. Standard-ocean conversion with unknown physical uncertainty remains approximate; do not turn latitude sensitivity into uncertainty or section-mean reversal into physical current-axis depth. Conditional circulation selections must remain separate.

For multi-jet observations distinguish the global branch maximum, vertically stacked secondary local maxima, and separate offshore filaments. A depth of a slower secondary maximum cannot replace the depth of the stronger near-surface maximum. An author near-surface support band may include an unsampled layer descriptively; do not turn it into a measured zero-depth point or a physical upper boundary. Upstream northern-ACC transition context is not complete downstream Malvinas coverage.

A source-reconstructed monthly regional velocity series may support separately typed current-following calendar-mean sampled core and isotach descriptors. Preserve the horizontal-axis operator, calendar contributor set at every retained depth, source depth limits, deep statistical extension, current direction, threshold, native interpolation brackets and shallow-edge flags. Do not conflate the crossing of a mean profile with mean crossing depths, product limit with bottom, source velocity standard error with depth error, or multiple derived metrics with independent observations.
